examples.text: Hoy hemos dado matemáticas en clase.
examples.translation: Today we had mathematics in class.

senses.definition_en: to pretend to be, to present oneself as though one were

examples.english: She pretends to be a nurse, but she's never studied (for it).
examples.text: Se las da de enfermera, pero nunca ha estudiado (para ello).
examples.translation: She pretends to be a nurse, but she's never studied (for it).

glosses: to pretend to be, to present oneself as though one were

senses.definition_en: to have a feeling/hunch/intuition

examples.english: I feel like they're not going to come.
examples.text: Me da que no van a venir.
examples.translation: I feel like they're not going to come.

glosses: to have a feeling/hunch/intuition

senses.definition_en: describes how good someone (the indirect object of the sentence) is at something; be ... at

examples.english: I'm really good at soccer/football, but I'm so-so at basketball.
examples.text: Se me da muy bien el fútbol, pero el baloncesto se me da más o menos. Literally, “Football gives itself to me very well, but basketball gives itself to me more or less”
examples.translation: I'm really good at soccer/football, but I'm so-so at basketball.

glosses: describes how good someone (the indirect object of the sentence) is at something; be ... at

senses.definition_en: to feel like doing something

examples.english: The other day I felt like going for a walk and I ran into Juan.
examples.text: El otro día me dio por salir a caminar y me topé con Juan.
examples.translation: The other day I felt like going for a walk and I ran into Juan.

glosses: to feel like doing something
